# Security Status

**Current release: `2.28.0`.** Every advisory published against this project is fixed as of `2.28.0`, and every one has a named regression test that runs in CI.

Installing `>= 2.28.0` clears every known advisory; `2.28.0` is the supported line and the one that receives fixes. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md#supported-versions).

25 advisories have been published and fixed (6 critical, 14 high, 5 medium). They are listed here in full, oldest patch first, because the count is less informative than the pattern: almost all of them are two defects — a caller-supplied path reaching a filesystem sink, and a caller-supplied target reaching the network — found one module at a time.

## How the recurrence was stopped

Fixing these individually did not converge. The guards were centralized and correct; what was missing was any check that modules *called* them, so each wave closed the modules that had been reported and left the ones that had not.

Both boundaries now have a registry-wide coverage test that fails the build rather than a convention that relies on reviewers:

| Boundary | Enforced by | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filesystem | [`test_write_sink_coverage.py`](tests/core/test_write_sink_coverage.py) | 88 modules declare a path parameter: 71 reach the guard, 17 are documented as not filesystem paths, 0 unaccounted |
| Outbound network | [`test_outbound_guard_coverage.py`](tests/core/test_outbound_guard_coverage.py) | 57 modules declare a URL/host parameter: 46 reach a guard, 11 are documented as never reaching the network, 0 unaccounted |

Exemptions must state what the parameter really addresses, and they are re-verified on every run: a module excused as "makes no request" fails the moment it opens a connection, and one excused for validating locally fails the moment that validation is removed.

Applying those audits closed roughly 30 further modules that no advisory had named. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the environment variables that define both boundaries.
